'''Egor Vladimirovich Demin''' (Russian: Егор Владимирович Демин; born 3 March 2006) is a Russian [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]]. He previously played for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].

==Early life==
Demin was born on 3 March 2006.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Egor-Demin/617738|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|title=Egor Demin}}</ref><ref name="auto3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.heraldextra.com/sports/byu/2024/jun/17/on-his-way-russian-star-egor-demin-officially-signs-with-byu-mens-basketball/|newspaper=[[Daily Herald (Utah)|Daily Herald]]|title=On his way: Russian star Egor Demin officially signs with BYU men’s basketball|date=17 June 2024|author=Dickson, Darnell}}</ref> His father, Vladimir, was also a basketball player.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://30-under-30.forbes.ru/2024/510307-egor-demin|website=[[Forbes|Forbes Russia]]|title=Егор Демин, 18 {{!}} Номинация «Спорт и киберспорт|language=Russian|trans-title=Egor Demin, 18 {{!}} Nomination “Sports and eSports”|date=2024}}</ref> He grew up in [[Moscow]] and attended the Moscow Basketball Academy (also known as the Trinta School) where he trained until 2021.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://mba.mossport.ru/news/egor-demin-chempion-yunosheskoy-evroligi/|website=MosSport.ru|title=Егор Демин - чемпион юношеской Евролиги!|date=22 May 2023|trans-title=Egor Demin is the champion of the Junior Euroleague!|language=Russian}}</ref> He received offers to play with other teams, including [[BC Khimki]], but opted to stay at the academy until age 15 to be with his coach, Evgeny Gorbunov.<ref name="auto1"/>

Demin had sent highlight footage to European teams and had received six offers by 2021.<ref name="auto1"/> He was considered a top Russian prospect and signed a six-year contract with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in September 2021, at age 15.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.defensacentral.com/baloncesto/1630589830-oficial-el-real-madrid-ha-fichado-al-mayor-talento-de-rusia-el-joven-egor-demin|website=DefensaCentral.com|title=Oficial: el Real Madrid ha fichado al mayor talento de Rusia, el joven Egor Demin|date=2 September 2021|author=Casado, Ramón|language=Spanish|trans-title=Official: Real Madrid has signed the greatest talent in Russia, the young Egor Demin}}</ref> Playing for the cadet "A" team in the Real Madrid academy, he helped them win the Spanish Cadet Championship in 2022 while averaging 17.3 points and 4.3 rebounds in the tournament.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sport-express.ru/basketball/euroleague/reviews/basketbol-kto-takoy-egor-demin-luchshiy-rossiyskiy-igrok-posle-kirilenko-skolko-emu-let-1931313/|newspaper=[[Sport Express]]|title="Его лично курирует агент Дончича". Российский разыгрывающий зажигает в "Реале"|date=26 May 2022|author=Ganeev, Timur|language=Russian|trans-title=“He is personally supervised by Doncic’s agent.” Russian point guard lights up Real Madrid}}</ref> For the following two seasons, he was a member of the junior "A" team and the [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B]] team in the [[Tercera FEB|Liga EBA]].<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/06/11/byu-recruit-egor-demin-byu-star-traveled-similar-paths/|newspaper=[[Deseret News]]|title=BYU’s former Russian basketball star sees big things ahead for Cougars’ top prospect|date=11 June 2024|author=McCann, Dave}}</ref>

Demin helped Real Madrid B to the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] championship in 2023 and scored 10 points in the final, while finishing with averages of 8.5 points and 6.8 rebounds per game.<ref name="auto"/> In May 2023, he received a promotion to the main Real Madrid squad and made his debut at the age of 17, playing in one game.<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/242530/egor-demin|website=Proballers.com|title=Egor Demin}}</ref> With Real Madrid B in the 2023–24 season, he played 21 games and averaged 13 points and 5.1 rebounds per game.<ref name="auto3"/> He also helped Real Madrid B return to the Next Generation Tournament and scored double figures in all four games, including 26 points and 11 rebounds in the final, an 85–84 overtime win over the French academy [[INSEP]].<ref name="auto3"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports.ru/basketball/1116097542-egor-demin-stal-dvukratnym-chempionom-yuniorskoj-evroligi.html|website=Sports.ru|title=Егор Демин стал двукратным чемпионом юниорской Евролиги|language=Russian|trans-title=Egor Demin became a two-time champion of the Junior Euroleague|date=26 May 2024|author=Ilyin, Gennady}}</ref>

In 2024, Demin was one of the nominees for the Russian [[Forbes 30 Under 30|''Forbes'' 30 Under 30]] list.<ref name="auto1"/>

===Recruiting===
Following the 2023–24 season, Demin opted to move to the U.S. to play [[college basketball]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/byu/basketball/international-nba-prospect-egor-demin-commits-to-byu-basketball|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=International NBA Prospect Egor Demin Commits to BYU Basketball|date=28 May 2024|author=Lundquist, Casey}}</ref> He committed to playing college basketball for [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]], where he was the program’s first five-star recruit,<ref>https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/08/02/byu-egor-demin-five-star/</ref> being described as "arguably the most notable prospect ever to commit to the BYU basketball program."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/06/02/egor-demin-announces-commitment-to-byu-basketball/|newspaper=[[Deseret News]]|title=‘Let’s rock BYU’: Russian star Egor Demin announces his commitment to the Cougars basketball program|date=2 June 2024|author=McDonald, Ryan}}</ref>

==National team career==
Demin represented Russia at the [[2021 FIBA U16 European Challengers]] tournament where he had per-40-minute averages of 21.1 points and 6.9 rebounds.<ref name="auto4">{{Cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/09/17/nba/1631870761_527152.html|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|title=Real Madrid's Demin, Duru among youngsters tipped for NBA|date=17 September 2021|author=Faucha, Fernando}}</ref> His performance at the tournament received comparisons to [[Luka Dončić]] by [[ESPN]] journalist Mike Schmitz.<ref name="auto4"/>
